101	(`LAZY`) buys nothing net; the row max's 7 points are its dependent
102	chain, and `MAX_TREE` buys nothing net either. **The floor of this loop
103	structure is 81% per clock with real loads.**
104	
105	**The memory side** (`L0_LOADS`: every K and V fragment load reads the
106	first key block, so the loads are issued and waited for as before but
107	every one is an L0 hit; wrong by construction, timed):
108	
109	| | real loads | `L0_LOADS` | |
110	|---|---:|---:|---|
111	| shipped (spilled) | 194.9 | 189.3 | 3%: the scratch reloads are not K/V |
112	| `QLDS TAIL_SPLIT PV_ORDER MAX_TREE LAZY` | 197.5 | **173.8** | **12%**, 41.9 TFLOP/s, 82% |
113	| `GUT_SOFTMAX` | 179.7 | 168.4 | 43.3, 85% |
114	| the floor | 176.3 | **162.4** | **44.8, 87.5%** |
115	| 768p, the same four | 1.192 / 1.175 / 1.109 / 1.114 s | 1.060 / 1.029 / 0.963 / **0.933** s | floor + L0: **45.0 TFLOP/s, 90%** |
116	
117	The decomposition of the spill-free kernel at 480p: **K/V loads 12
118	points, softmax 6, the in-wave floor 82–87%** (128 fragment loads, 130
119	allocator moves and 80 address adds beside 128 MMAs). That is the GEMM's
120	G1 picture again — ~10 memory points, then the schedule — and the lever
121	that took the GEMM's memory points was §2.9: the slab fetched once a
122	workgroup a block ahead and shared through LDS at wave32.
123	
124	#### What that lever would take here, and why it was not built today
125	
126	A workgroup of W waves sharing each key block's K and V tiles (32 KB a
127	block at KTIL4, head 128). Staging a block ahead through registers, as
128	§2.9 does, costs 32 KB / (32 W) bytes a lane: 32 VGPRs at W = 8, which
129	does not fit beside `QT2`'s 128 accumulators (the shipped build is at 256
130	with 112 spilled), so the wave drops to `QT1` (O^T 64, S^T 32, P^T 32,
131	staging 32: ~190) and reads four `ds_load_b64` a fragment at one fragment
132	an MMA — twice the GEMM's ratio, whose reads §2.10 priced at 3%, so ~6 —
133	plus a barrier a block (the GEMM's barrier-and-reads together were 9). Net
134	expected: the 12 memory points less 6–9, on a kernel that is 33% of a
135	video forward: **≤ 2% of a forward for a session's build.** Decision 7's
136	plateau is reached on the exact arms (five consecutive inside ±2%), so
137	this is recorded as the one structural lever left (G4b) and not built.
138	
139	**Dead by arithmetic, so not built:** a head-dimension split (S^T needs
140	all 128 channels, so two passes of 64 recompute it: 1.5x the MMAs);
141	wave64 for the transposed kernel (a VALU instruction is two passes at
142	wave64 and the softmax is 7 VALU an MMA; A/B fragments move 4x their
143	bytes; §6.2 measured the plain kernel 1.40x slower at wave64 for the same
144	reasons, and G-o4's element order is moot).
145	
146	#### The carry-in: the image DiT (opt-in, held by the edit gate)
147	
148	`qimage/dit` runs `dit_attention_wmma.comp` (`QT1 KTIL4`, wave32, fp32
149	context out) and then a "narrow ctx" pass to fp16. It can now run
150	`qimage_attn_t_qt2_kt4` (`h3_attn_t.comp`, `STORE_TAIL=0`) instead:
151	`QIMAGE_ATTN_T=1` at process start, the element order probed at the first
152	graph through `h3/dit.TransposedAttentionOK` (staging still submits
153	nothing), the context written fp16 at the output projection's stride, and
154	"narrow ctx" kept only for the causal text passes' rows in an edit
155	prefill. `STORE_TAIL=0` gained the bound the plain kernel's fp32 store
156	has: the tile the sequence ends inside is stored one query a lane (each
157	lane owns a query outright), because the edit prefill repairs the prefix
158	one segment at a time with the key count cut to the segment's end, and
159	a whole-tile store past that end overwrote the next segment's finished
160	rows. The video VAE's five head-64 builds carry the same bound
161	(`TestGPUDecoder`: PSNR 81.7 dB, unchanged).
162	
163	`TestGPUStepProfile`, 1024² (4,096 image rows + the prompt), the int8
164	bank:
165	
166	| | attention, 32 layers | TFLOP/s | a cached step | a prefill |
167	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
168	| plain `QT1 KTIL4` wave32 (the default) | 248 ms | 35.7 | 1.908 s | 1.966 s |
169	| **transposed `QT2 KTIL4`** (`QIMAGE_ATTN_T=1`) | **232 ms** | **38.3** | **1.876 s** | 1.934 s |
170	
171	1.07x on the kernel, not H3's 1.55x: the image DiT's plain kernel was
172	already at 35.7 on its 4k-key sequences where H3's plain build reads 24
173	at 16k.
174	
175	**The gates.** `TestGPUOracle256` and `TestGPUOracle1024` (40
176	teacher-forced and free-running steps) pass on the transposed build.
177	**`TestGPUEditOracle` does not**: the teacher-forced prefill reads rel
178	7.9e-2 against its 2e-2 bound (rms 2.4e-3, 0.41x the released bf16
179	pipeline's own error), where the plain kernel reads 7.7e-3; the cached
180	steps after it are the plain kernel's (6e-4, 9e-4, 2.4e-4), and the
181	free-running four steps end at rel 1.5e-2 (rms 4e-3) against the plain
182	kernel's 2.2e-3. Where it comes from, block by block (the fp16 context
183	plane dumped after block N's attention under each kernel, the same
184	inputs, the same step):
185	
186	| | rms rel | max rel | note |
187	|---|---:|---:|---|
188	| block 0, transposed against plain | **8.1e-5** | 1.5e-4 | fp16 rounding, H3's 9.7e-5; the causal text rows identical |
189	| block 19, transposed **at that block only**, plain everywhere before it | **1.1e-4** | 2.4e-4 | the kernel on identical inputs: exact |
190	| blocks 10 / 15 / 16 / 17 / 18 / 19 / 20, transposed throughout | | 6e-4 / 1.4e-3 / 1.6e-3 / 1.1e-2 / 1.5e-2 / 2.3e-2 / **1.7e-1** | target rows 288, 304, 513 (image rows 0–1 and 14, columns 11–12); the prefix rows stay at ≤ 1.6e-3 |
191	| the plain `QT1 KTIL8` wave64 build on the main pass (a plain-family fp16 perturbation of the target rows) | | 7e-5 → 3e-3 by block 30 | the gate reads 8.4e-3 |
192	| the same build on the prefix passes (the prefix rows perturbed instead) | | | the gate reads **1.73e-2** |
193	| transposed main pass only / prefix passes only / both | | | 1.74e-2 / 1.06e-2 / **7.9e-2** |
194	
195	So the kernel is exact at the fp16 level at every block on identical
196	inputs, and this edit's prefill amplifies an fp16-level difference in the
197	*prefix* rows ~100x at three target rows between blocks 16 and 20: a
198	perturbation from the plain kernel's own family lands at 1.73e-2 against
199	the 2e-2 bound, and the transposed kernel's, ~3x larger at the kernel
200	(8.1e-5 against 2.7e-5 rms), at 7.9e-2. The gate is within 2x of its
201	sensitivity floor for edits, and it is the vertical's gate, so **the
202	transposed kernel is opt-in for the image DiT, not the default**: 1.7% of
203	a step, held until the image vertical decides whether its edit bound
204	measures the kernel or the input. Nothing served changes.
205	
206	Not carried: `ace/dit`'s full attention (grouped-query heads, which
207	`h3_attn_t.comp` does not map; its attention is a small share of a music
208	step), the speech encoders (short clips, tiny), the VAE's exact arms
209	(spill-free already; the same knobs apply and were not screened).
210

212	`Q_LPITCH`, `PV_ORDER`, `MAX_TREE`, `LAZY` (exact), and the controls
213	`L0_LOADS`, `GUT_CORR/EXP/MAX/SOFTMAX/XCHG` (wrong by construction); the
214	key block is `shaders/h3_attn_t_block.glsl`, included once for whole
215	blocks and once for the tail. The default build's ISA is unchanged (the
216	restructure is a no-op without the knobs: the SPIR-V differs only in its

218	second and reports "bits: identical" per arm. Screens:

H3_ATTN_ONLY_SPV=1 H3_ATTN_SPV=qt:ktil:path,…`), block 49's planes after
a real forward, 15,936 keys, the shipped build and every arm in the same
run, the sampler beside it (2650–2690 MHz at 154 W, so the ceiling is
~51.2 TFLOP/s). The screen now checks every loaded arm bit for bit
against the shipped transposed build ("bits: identical"), which is the
gate for a scheduling arm. Three runs of the shipped build: 192.6 /
195.0 / 194.9 ms.

**The exact arms** (all bit-identical to the shipped build):

| arm (`-D` on `h3_attn_t.comp`) | VGPRs / spilled | 480p, ms | |
|---|---|---:|---|
| shipped `QT2 KTIL4` | 256 / 112 | **192.6 – 195.0** | 37.3–37.8 TFLOP/s, 73% |
| `TAIL_SPLIT` (the last block peeled out of the loop: no mask arithmetic in whole blocks, −111 VALU) | 256 / 112 | 201.3 – 207.6 | −4% |
| `QLDS` (Q^T in 8 KB of LDS, no spill) | 256 / 0 | 204.0 | −5% |
| `QLDS TAIL_SPLIT` | 256 / 0 | 202.1 | |
| `QLDS Q_LPITCH=24` | 256 / 0 | 223.0 | 3 subgroups a SIMD |
| `QREG=0 TAIL_SPLIT` (Q^T re-read from memory) | 256 / 0 | 206.5 | |
| `QT2 KTIL2`, `QT1 KTIL4`, `QT1 KTIL8` with `QLDS TAIL_SPLIT` | 256 / 0, 192 / 0, 216 / 0 | 203.8, 337.4, 281.1 | QT1 pays two fragment loads an MMA |
| `MAX_TREE` (the row max as a balanced tree) | 256 / 112 | 200.6 | |
| `LAZY` (the rescale skipped when no lane's max moved: corr is exactly 1) | 256 / 112 | 201.0 | |
| `PV_ORDER` (P^T built a key tile at a time, its MMAs behind it; peak live set ~24 VGPRs smaller) | 256 / 112 | 209.9 | |
| `QLDS TAIL_SPLIT PV_ORDER` | 256 / 0 | 193.3 / 194.6 | |
| **`QLDS TAIL_SPLIT PV_ORDER MAX_TREE LAZY`** | 256 / 0 | **192.7 / 197.5** | 776 VALU, 239 moves, no reloads: **the same time** |
| `QLDS TAIL_SPLIT MAX_TREE LAZY` | 256 / 0 | 193.8 / 195.8 | |

At 768p (38,247 keys, ~2600 MHz): shipped 1.192 s (35.2), the best arm
1.175 s (35.7). The two builds execute 135 fewer VALU and 113 fewer
reloads a block for the same time, so **the instruction count is not the
price** on this kernel (as §2.13 found on the MoE GEMM): with 4–5 waves
a SIMD one wave's VALU overlaps another's MMAs, and what a source change
does to the allocation — `TAIL_SPLIT` alone adds 70 `v_swap` a block for
its −111 VALU — is as large as what it saves.

**The honest gutting** (each phase removed with its result kept live: P^T
still feeds the MMAs, O^T is still stored), on the spill-free
`QLDS TAIL_SPLIT` base (202.1 ms):

| taken away | ms | of the base |
|---|---:|---:|
| the online rescale of O^T (`GUT_CORR`) | 196.3 | 3% |
| the exp2 (`GUT_EXP`) | 199.9 | 1% |
| the row max (`GUT_MAX`) | 187.3 | 7% |
| the whole softmax, exchange kept (`GUT_SOFTMAX`) | 180.1 / 179.7 | **11%** |
| … and the exchange (`GUT_XCHG`): MMAs and loads alone | 178.7 / 176.3 | 12–13%; **41.3 TFLOP/s, 81% per clock** |

So A2 (lazy rescaling) is bounded at 3 points and the exact version of it
(`LAZY`) buys nothing net; the row max's 7 points are its dependent
chain, and `MAX_TREE` buys nothing net either. **The floor of this loop
structure is 81% per clock with real loads.**

**The memory side** (`L0_LOADS`: every K and V fragment load reads the
first key block, so the loads are issued and waited for as before but
every one is an L0 hit; wrong by construction, timed):

| | real loads | `L0_LOADS` | |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| shipped (spilled) | 194.9 | 189.3 | 3%: the scratch reloads are not K/V |
| `QLDS TAIL_SPLIT PV_ORDER MAX_TREE LAZY` | 197.5 | **173.8** | **12%**, 41.9 TFLOP/s, 82% |
| `GUT_SOFTMAX` | 179.7 | 168.4 | 43.3, 85% |
| the floor | 176.3 | **162.4** | **44.8, 87.5%** |
| 768p, the same four | 1.192 / 1.175 / 1.109 / 1.114 s | 1.060 / 1.029 / 0.963 / **0.933** s | floor + L0: **45.0 TFLOP/s, 90%** |

The decomposition of the spill-free kernel at 480p: **K/V loads 12
points, softmax 6, the in-wave floor 82–87%** (128 fragment loads, 130
allocator moves and 80 address adds beside 128 MMAs). That is the GEMM's
G1 picture again — ~10 memory points, then the schedule — and the lever
that took the GEMM's memory points was §2.9: the slab fetched once a
workgroup a block ahead and shared through LDS at wave32.

#### What that lever would take here, and why it was not built today

A workgroup of W waves sharing each key block's K and V tiles (32 KB a
block at KTIL4, head 128). Staging a block ahead through registers, as
§2.9 does, costs 32 KB / (32 W) bytes a lane: 32 VGPRs at W = 8, which
does not fit beside `QT2`'s 128 accumulators (the shipped build is at 256
with 112 spilled), so the wave drops to `QT1` (O^T 64, S^T 32, P^T 32,
staging 32: ~190) and reads four `ds_load_b64` a fragment at one fragment
an MMA — twice the GEMM's ratio, whose reads §2.10 priced at 3%, so ~6 —
plus a barrier a block (the GEMM's barrier-and-reads together were 9). Net
expected: the 12 memory points less 6–9, on a kernel that is 33% of a
video forward: **≤ 2% of a forward for a session's build.** Decision 7's
plateau is reached on the exact arms (five consecutive inside ±2%), so
this is recorded as the one structural lever left (G4b) and not built.

**Dead by arithmetic, so not built:** a head-dimension split (S^T needs
all 128 channels, so two passes of 64 recompute it: 1.5x the MMAs);
wave64 for the transposed kernel (a VALU instruction is two passes at
wave64 and the softmax is 7 VALU an MMA; A/B fragments move 4x their
bytes; §6.2 measured the plain kernel 1.40x slower at wave64 for the same
reasons, and G-o4's element order is moot).

#### The carry-in: the image DiT (opt-in, held by the edit gate)

`qimage/dit` runs `dit_attention_wmma.comp` (`QT1 KTIL4`, wave32, fp32
context out) and then a "narrow ctx" pass to fp16. It can now run
`qimage_attn_t_qt2_kt4` (`h3_attn_t.comp`, `STORE_TAIL=0`) instead:
`QIMAGE_ATTN_T=1` at process start, the element order probed at the first
graph through `h3/dit.TransposedAttentionOK` (staging still submits
nothing), the context written fp16 at the output projection's stride, and
"narrow ctx" kept only for the causal text passes' rows in an edit
prefill. `STORE_TAIL=0` gained the bound the plain kernel's fp32 store
has: the tile the sequence ends inside is stored one query a lane (each
lane owns a query outright), because the edit prefill repairs the prefix
one segment at a time with the key count cut to the segment's end, and
a whole-tile store past that end overwrote the next segment's finished
rows. The video VAE's five head-64 builds carry the same bound
(`TestGPUDecoder`: PSNR 81.7 dB, unchanged).

`TestGPUStepProfile`, 1024² (4,096 image rows + the prompt), the int8
bank:

| | attention, 32 layers | TFLOP/s | a cached step | a prefill |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| plain `QT1 KTIL4` wave32 (the default) | 248 ms | 35.7 | 1.908 s | 1.966 s |
| **transposed `QT2 KTIL4`** (`QIMAGE_ATTN_T=1`) | **232 ms** | **38.3** | **1.876 s** | 1.934 s |

1.07x on the kernel, not H3's 1.55x: the image DiT's plain kernel was
already at 35.7 on its 4k-key sequences where H3's plain build reads 24
at 16k.

**The gates.** `TestGPUOracle256` and `TestGPUOracle1024` (40
teacher-forced and free-running steps) pass on the transposed build.
**`TestGPUEditOracle` does not**: the teacher-forced prefill reads rel
7.9e-2 against its 2e-2 bound (rms 2.4e-3, 0.41x the released bf16
pipeline's own error), where the plain kernel reads 7.7e-3; the cached
steps after it are the plain kernel's (6e-4, 9e-4, 2.4e-4), and the
free-running four steps end at rel 1.5e-2 (rms 4e-3) against the plain
kernel's 2.2e-3. Where it comes from, block by block (the fp16 context
plane dumped after block N's attention under each kernel, the same
inputs, the same step):

| | rms rel | max rel | note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| block 0, transposed against plain | **8.1e-5** | 1.5e-4 | fp16 rounding, H3's 9.7e-5; the causal text rows identical |
| block 19, transposed **at that block only**, plain everywhere before it | **1.1e-4** | 2.4e-4 | the kernel on identical inputs: exact |
| blocks 10 / 15 / 16 / 17 / 18 / 19 / 20, transposed throughout | | 6e-4 / 1.4e-3 / 1.6e-3 / 1.1e-2 / 1.5e-2 / 2.3e-2 / **1.7e-1** | target rows 288, 304, 513 (image rows 0–1 and 14, columns 11–12); the prefix rows stay at ≤ 1.6e-3 |
| the plain `QT1 KTIL8` wave64 build on the main pass (a plain-family fp16 perturbation of the target rows) | | 7e-5 → 3e-3 by block 30 | the gate reads 8.4e-3 |
| the same build on the prefix passes (the prefix rows perturbed instead) | | | the gate reads **1.73e-2** |
| transposed main pass only / prefix passes only / both | | | 1.74e-2 / 1.06e-2 / **7.9e-2** |

So the kernel is exact at the fp16 level at every block on identical
inputs, and this edit's prefill amplifies an fp16-level difference in the
*prefix* rows ~100x at three target rows between blocks 16 and 20: a
perturbation from the plain kernel's own family lands at 1.73e-2 against
the 2e-2 bound, and the transposed kernel's, ~3x larger at the kernel
(8.1e-5 against 2.7e-5 rms), at 7.9e-2. The gate is within 2x of its
sensitivity floor for edits, and it is the vertical's gate, so **the
transposed kernel is opt-in for the image DiT, not the default**: 1.7% of
a step, held until the image vertical decides whether its edit bound
measures the kernel or the input. Nothing served changes.

Not carried: `ace/dit`'s full attention (grouped-query heads, which
`h3_attn_t.comp` does not map; its attention is a small share of a music
step), the speech encoders (short clips, tiny), the VAE's exact arms
(spill-free already; the same knobs apply and were not screened).

**Tools left in the tree:** on `h3_attn_t.comp`, `TAIL_SPLIT`, `QLDS` /
`Q_LPITCH`, `PV_ORDER`, `MAX_TREE`, `LAZY` (exact), and the controls
`L0_LOADS`, `GUT_CORR/EXP/MAX/SOFTMAX/XCHG` (wrong by construction); the
key block is `shaders/h3_attn_t_block.glsl`, included once for whole
blocks and once for the tail. The default build's ISA is unchanged (the
restructure is a no-op without the knobs: the SPIR-V differs only in its
ID bound). `H3_ATTN_ONLY_SPV` now puts the shipped transposed build
second and reports "bits: identical" per arm. Screens:
`scratchpad/screen{1,2,3,768}.samples` for the clocks.

| **`LDS_STAGE` at wave32 4×4, pitch 36, one tile a slab** | 8 waves, 240 VGPRs | **40.7** | **78%** | |
| **… two tiles a slab** | 256 VGPRs, 54 KB | **40.9**, o 39.4 | **79%** | **shipped** |
| the wave32 control: 4×4, direct loads, no LDS | 192 VGPRs | 21.5 | 40% | wave32 alone is a disaster: a tile is 272 clocks of MMA and the latency is the same |
| `STAGE_L0`: the staging loads all L0 hits (wrong by construction) | | 44.0 | 82% | **the global side is now ~3 points**; the rest is the LDS-side schedule |
| `LOAD_ORDER`: reads issued A0, B0..B3, A1.. so the first MMA waits for the 2nd fragment, not the 5th | | 40.6 | 79% | nothing |

**What it says.**

1. **A wave64 fragment is 8 VGPRs, not 2.** The hardware holds an A or
   B operand four times over (lanes 16–31, 32–47 and 48–63 replicate
   0–15; `coopmat_layout_probe.comp`), so a prefetched *fragment* costs
   4x its bytes in registers and 4x its bytes on the L0-to-VGPR path,
   which is why §6.5's "+24 VGPRs" was +96 and why no register-resident
   prefetch fits beside a 4×8 accumulator grid. At wave32 the replication
   is 2x. A prefetched *slab* costs each byte once, in 24 staging
   registers.
2. **ACO will not carry a fragment across a loop back-edge.** Both
   register-prefetch arms compiled to hundreds of sub-dword moves a
   trip (a coopmat is a vector of 16-bit elements, and a phi it cannot
   coalesce is copied element by element). Any cross-iteration register
   pipelining of cooperative-matrix operands is dead on Mesa 26.2.2, and
   a build that carries none (a hoisted multi-tile slab, or LDS) is the
   only shape that measures the idea. `PIPE` and `DB` stay in
   `dit_gemm.comp` as the record of that, never built.
3. **LDS reads of a cooperative matrix are `ds_load_b64`**, whatever the
   alignment, so the conflict-free pitch is 18 dwords (36 halves) apart
   between the 16 lanes of a fragment, not the 12 (24 halves) that a
   128-bit read would want. §2.1's LDS arms had no pad at all (a pitch
   of 8 dwords, 4-way conflicted) and an [N, K] B gather; that is why
   they lost by 1.2x in 2026-09-14, and it was not the mechanism.
4. **Wave32 and the LDS are one lever, not two.** Wave32 halves the
   bytes every fragment read moves and doubles the accumulator's
   registers, so its largest tile is 4×4 (AI 32) and, fed from global
   memory, its 272-clock tiles expose the same latency four times as
   often: 21.5 TFLOP/s. Fed from LDS a slab ahead, the latency is the
   LDS's and the 4×4 tile's extra bytes go down a path that is not the
   L0's: 40.9.
5. **The gap left is the LDS-side schedule** (~18 points at the clock):
   with the staging loads perfect the kernel reaches 82%; the shipped
   build 79–80%. A slab is 32 MMAs (544 clocks a wave), 64 `ds_load_b64`,
   6 `ds_store`, a barrier and a `lgkmcnt` ladder whose first MMA waits
   for 20 of 64 reads; the issue order of the reads does not move it.
   Where the next 5 points are is open (KERNELS.md G-o8).

**Carry-in (KERNELS.md G8, the same day).** All nine hosts run it,
pinned to wave32 through a `wave` field on each variant table, each
through its own gate: the image DiT's 1024² step 2179 → 2058 ms (one
staging, five arms), the video VAE's 480p decode 37.1 → 35.5 s (its
bias-padded K rounded to 32), Kev's fp16 pass at 494 tokens 154 → 132
ms. **It loses under ~40 workgroups**: ACE's 30 s clip (375 rows, 30
workgroups) is 130 against the wave64 build's 120 ms a forward, ties at
1500 rows, wins 2.5–3% from 3000, so `ace/dit` keeps the wave64 build up
to 1024 rows; parakeet's rung at 138–768 frames loses 8–11%, and its plan
never picks it.

**Reproduce.** The builds are `go generate` lines in `shaders/shaders.go`
(`dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32`, `_krange`); the ladder's arms are
`-DSR`, `-DPIPE`, `-DDB`, `-DLDS_STAGE` with `-DA_LPITCH`/`-DB_LPITCH`,
`-DSTAGE_L0`, `-DLOAD_ORDER` on `dit_gemm.comp`, compiled to the
scratchpad. The screen: `H3_SHAPES=480 H3_PROFILE=1 H3_BANK=q8
H3_GEMM_SPV=path [H3_GEMM_WAVE=32] [H3_GEMM_KRANGE_SPV=path]
H3_GEMM_REF=ref.bits go test ./h3/dit -run TestGPUShapes -v`, where the
first run writes the velocities' bits and every later one is gated on
them; the clock and power from a 100 ms sampler on
`hwmon/freq1_input` and `power1_average` (§0.6). The ISA:
`RADV_DEBUG=asm,shaderstats go run ./cmd/probe build.spv 32`.

389	// the shipped build shows ACO hoisting the next tile's six staging loads

399	#endif

401	#define KT_LOOP 0
402	#endif

410	// construction. Only the first STORE_TILES of a wave's WM*WN accumulator
411	// tiles are stored; the rest are stored under a condition that is never
412	// true at run time (pc.gemmK == 0) and that the compiler cannot decide, so
413	// every MMA stays and only the epilogue's stores go. At 0 the K loop runs

438	// Four dwords into the uint planes (base in uints).
439	#define PUT4(arr, base, v) {                                                   \
440	    arr[(base) + 0u] = (v).x; arr[(base) + 1u] = (v).y;                        \
441	    arr[(base) + 2u] = (v).z; arr[(base) + 3u] = (v).w;                        \
442	}
443	// Eight halves of a packed uvec4 into elements [b, b+8) of a fragment.
444	#define PUT8(f, b, v) {                                                        \
445	    f16vec2 h0 = unpackFloat2x16((v).x), h1 = unpackFloat2x16((v).y);          \
446	    f16vec2 h2 = unpackFloat2x16((v).z), h3 = unpackFloat2x16((v).w);          \
447	    f[(b) + 0] = h0.x; f[(b) + 1] = h0.y; f[(b) + 2] = h1.x; f[(b) + 3] = h1.y; \
448	    f[(b) + 4] = h2.x; f[(b) + 5] = h2.y; f[(b) + 6] = h3.x; f[(b) + 7] = h3.y; \
449	}
450	// One fragment out of a plane: `at` is this lane's uint index of its eight
451	// halves (the row's or column's base, plus 4 for lanes 16..31).
452	#define XCHG_FRAG(T, arr, at, out) {                                           \
453	    uvec4 mine = uvec4(arr[at], arr[(at) + 1u], arr[(at) + 2u], arr[(at) + 3u]); \
454	    uvec4 other = subgroupShuffleXor(mine, 16u);                               \
455	    bool low = gl_SubgroupInvocationID < 16u;                                  \
456	    uvec4 lo = low ? mine : other, hi = low ? other : mine;                    \
457	    T f;                                                                       \
458	    PUT8(f, 0, lo)                                                             \
459	    PUT8(f, 8, hi)                                                             \
460	    out = f;                                                                   \
461	}

464	shared float16_t lsB[2 * B_PLANE];

467	// ds_store_b128 (gemm_wmma.comp verified it in the disassembly).
468	#define SPREAD8(arr, base, v) {                                                \
469	    f16vec2 h0 = unpackFloat2x16((v).x);                                       \
470	    f16vec2 h1 = unpackFloat2x16((v).y);                                       \
471	    f16vec2 h2 = unpackFloat2x16((v).z);                                       \
472	    f16vec2 h3 = unpackFloat2x16((v).w);                                       \
473	    arr[(base) + 0u] = h0.x; arr[(base) + 1u] = h0.y;                          \
474	    arr[(base) + 2u] = h1.x; arr[(base) + 3u] = h1.y;                          \
475	    arr[(base) + 4u] = h2.x; arr[(base) + 5u] = h2.y;                          \
476	    arr[(base) + 6u] = h3.x; arr[(base) + 7u] = h3.y;                          \
477	}
478	#endif

498	        + (((k0) + (kt) * TILE) >> pc.aux2) * pc.aux1                              \

527	// A: [M, lda], K-contiguous, row-major fragment load.
528	#define LOAD_FRAG_A(dst, i, k0, kt)                                            \
529	    coopMatLoad(dst, hact, pc.inOff + (wm0 + (i) * TILE) * pc.lda + (k0) + (kt) * TILE, \

531	#endif
532	#ifndef L0_LOADS
533	#define L0_LOADS 0
534	#endif

537	#define LOAD_FRAG_B(dst, j, k0, kt)                                            \

550	    coopMatLoad(dst, w16, bAt[j] + (kt) * TILE * pc.ldb, pc.ldb, gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);

552	#define B_STEP (BK_TILES * TILE * TILE)

554	    coopMatLoad(dst, w16, bAt[j] + (kt) * (TILE * TILE), TILE, gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutColumnMajor);

556	#define LOAD_FRAG_B(dst, j, k0, kt)                                            \
557	    coopMatLoad(dst, w16, pc.bOff + (wn0 + (j) * TILE) * pc.ldb + (k0) + (kt) * TILE, \

565	    coopMatLoad(dst, w16, pc.bOff +                                            \
566	        (((wn0 + (j) * TILE) / TILE) * (pc.gemmK / TILE) + (((k0) & 16u) / TILE)) * (TILE * TILE), \
567	        TILE, gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutColumnMajor);

569	// Tile (nt, kt) is one contiguous 512 B block, kt fastest, holding element
570	// (k, n) at n*TILE + k -- which is what a column-major load of stride TILE
571	// reads. pc.ldb is unused; the tile row is pc.gemmK / TILE tiles long.
572	#define LOAD_FRAG_B(dst, j, k0, kt)                                            \
573	    coopMatLoad(dst, w16, pc.bOff +                                            \
574	        (((wn0 + (j) * TILE) / TILE) * (pc.gemmK / TILE) + ((k0) + (kt) * TILE) / TILE) * (TILE * TILE), \

578	// One K-slab: WM A-fragments and WN B-fragments per K-tile, then WM*WN MMAs
579	// against them. With HOIST_A the slab's A loads all issue before the first
580	// MMA, so the wave has BK_TILES*32 bytes of each A row outstanding at once
581	// instead of 32 (§5.1b mechanism 3, §2.7).
582	#if HOIST_A
583	#define MMA_BLOCK(k0) {                                                        \
584	    FRAG_A_T fragA[BK_TILES][WM];                                              \
585	    [[unroll]] for (uint kt = 0u; kt < BK_TILES; kt++) {                       \
586	        [[unroll]] for (uint i = 0u; i < WM; i++) { LOAD_FRAG_A(fragA[kt][i], i, k0, kt) } \
587	    }                                                                          \
588	    [[unroll]] for (uint kt = 0u; kt < BK_TILES; kt++) {                       \
589	        FRAG_B_T fragB[WN];                                                    \
590	        [[unroll]] for (uint j = 0u; j < WN; j++) { LOAD_FRAG_B(fragB[j], j, k0, kt) } \
591	        [[unroll]] for (uint i = 0u; i < WM; i++) {                            \
592	            [[unroll]] for (uint j = 0u; j < WN; j++) {                        \
593	                acc[i][j] = coopMatMulAdd(fragA[kt][i], fragB[j], acc[i][j]);  \
594	            }                                                                  \
595	        }                                                                      \
596	    }                                                                          \
597	}

599	// The slab's first tile's fragments, used for every tile (wrong by
600	// construction; the pricing arm above).
601	#define MMA_BLOCK(k0) {                                                        \
602	    FRAG_A_T fragA[WM];                                                        \
603	    FRAG_B_T fragB[WN];                                                        \
604	    [[unroll]] for (uint i = 0u; i < WM; i++) { LOAD_FRAG_A(fragA[i], i, k0, 0) } \
605	    [[unroll]] for (uint j = 0u; j < WN; j++) { LOAD_FRAG_B(fragB[j], j, k0, 0) } \
606	    [[unroll]] for (uint kt = 0u; kt < BK_TILES; kt++) {                       \
607	        [[unroll]] for (uint i = 0u; i < WM; i++) {                            \
608	            [[unroll]] for (uint j = 0u; j < WN; j++) {                        \
609	                acc[i][j] = coopMatMulAdd(fragA[i], fragB[j], acc[i][j]);      \
610	            }                                                                  \
611	        }                                                                      \
612	    }                                                                          \
613	}
614	#elif LOAD_ORDER
615	// The reads issued A0, B0..BWN-1, A1..: the first MMA (A0 x B0) waits for
616	// the second fragment to land instead of the (WM+1)th, and each A after
617	// that enables a row of MMAs as it arrives.
618	#if KT_LOOP
619	#define KT_UNROLL [[dont_unroll]]
620	#else
621	#define KT_UNROLL [[unroll]]
622	#endif
623	#define MMA_BLOCK(k0) {                                                        \
624	    KT_UNROLL for (uint kt = 0u; kt < BK_TILES; kt++) {                        \
625	        FRAG_A_T fragA[WM];                                                    \
626	        FRAG_B_T fragB[WN];                                                    \
627	        LOAD_FRAG_A(fragA[0], 0, k0, kt)                                       \
628	        [[unroll]] for (uint j = 0u; j < WN; j++) { LOAD_FRAG_B(fragB[j], j, k0, kt) } \
629	        [[unroll]] for (uint i = 1u; i < WM; i++) { LOAD_FRAG_A(fragA[i], i, k0, kt) } \
630	        [[unroll]] for (uint i = 0u; i < WM; i++) {                            \
631	            [[unroll]] for (uint j = 0u; j < WN; j++) {                        \
632	                acc[i][j] = coopMatMulAdd(fragA[i], fragB[j], acc[i][j]);      \
633	            }                                                                  \
634	        }                                                                      \
635	    }                                                                          \
636	}
637	#else
638	#if KT_LOOP
639	#define KT_UNROLL [[dont_unroll]]
640	#else
641	#define KT_UNROLL [[unroll]]
642	#endif
643	#define MMA_BLOCK(k0) {                                                        \
644	    KT_UNROLL for (uint kt = 0u; kt < BK_TILES; kt++) {                        \
645	        FRAG_A_T fragA[WM];                                                    \

647	        [[unroll]] for (uint i = 0u; i < WM; i++) { LOAD_FRAG_A(fragA[i], i, k0, kt) } \
648	        [[unroll]] for (uint j = 0u; j < WN; j++) { LOAD_FRAG_B(fragB[j], j, k0, kt) } \

684	    [[unroll]] for (uint i = 0u; i < WM; i++) {

692	            [[unroll]] for (uint j = 0u; j < WN; j++) {
693	                coopMatLoad(acc[i][j], act, pc.outOff + (wm0 + i * TILE) * pc.gemmN + wn0 + j * TILE,

696	        }

701	    // The tap's row offset and the column inside it, carried across the loop.
702	    // pc.aux0 is a multiple of BK, so the rollover is exact and a whole slab
703	    // is always inside one tap.
704	    uint aTap = 0u, aCol = 0u;
705	#endif

707	    const uint kStart = pc.aux0, kEnd = pc.aux1;
708	#else
709	    const uint kStart = 0u, kEnd = pc.gemmK;
710	#endif
711	#if SR
712	    // The fragment offsets, carried across the loop (see SR above).
713	    uint aAt[WM], bAt[WN];
714	    [[unroll]] for (uint i = 0u; i < WM; i++) {
715	        aAt[i] = pc.inOff + (wm0 + i * TILE) * pc.lda + kStart;
716	    }
717	    [[unroll]] for (uint j = 0u; j < WN; j++) {
718	#if B_LAYOUT == 0
719	        bAt[j] = pc.bOff + (wn0 + j * TILE) * pc.ldb + kStart;
720	#elif B_LAYOUT == 1
721	        bAt[j] = pc.bOff + kStart * pc.ldb + wn0 + j * TILE;
722	#else

726	#endif

728	    uint tid = gl_LocalInvocationID.x;
729	    uvec4 stageA[A_STAGE], stageB[B_STAGE];
730	    // Each lane's chunk of the slab: where it comes from (a uvec4 index into

732	    uint aG[A_STAGE], aL[A_STAGE], bG[B_STAGE], bL[B_STAGE];
733	    [[unroll]] for (uint s = 0u; s < A_STAGE; s++) {
734	        uint c = tid + s * NTHREADS;
735	        uint r = c / (BK / 8), col = (c % (BK / 8)) * 8u;

737	        aL[s] = r * A_LPITCH + col;
738	    }
739	    [[unroll]] for (uint s = 0u; s < B_STAGE; s++) {
740	        // Chunk c: tile (nt, kt) of the slab, 16-byte piece w of its 512.
741	        uint c = tid + s * NTHREADS;
742	        uint nt = c / (BK_TILES * TILE * TILE / 8);
743	        uint kt = (c / (TILE * TILE / 8)) % BK_TILES, w = c % (TILE * TILE / 8);

745	        bL[s] = nt * (TILE * B_LPITCH) + (w / 2u) * B_LPITCH + kt * TILE + (w % 2u) * 8u;
746	    }
747	#define LOAD_STAGE(back) {                                                     \
748	    [[unroll]] for (uint s = 0u; s < A_STAGE; s++) {                           \
749	        if (tid + s * NTHREADS < A_VECS) { stageA[s] = hact4[aG[s] - (back) * (BK / 8)]; } \

p='h3_attn_t.comp'
s=open(p).read()
old=s[s.index('    FETCH_K(0u)\n'):s.index('#else\n#define KV_AFTER_S\n')]
new='''    FETCH_K(0u)
    FETCH_V(0u)
    STORE_K
    STORE_V
    barrier();
    // A block fetches the next block's K at its top, in flight behind its
    // S^T MMAs, and writes it to the plane behind the barrier that ends
    // their reads; then V likewise behind the softmax and the O^T MMAs.
    // Fetched and stored inside one trip: a staging register carried across
    // the back-edge is copied there, behind a wait for the fetch (the
    // first cut's disassembly, research/3.9). At the last block the fetches
    // re-read it (in bounds, never read back).
#define KV_BEFORE_S { FETCH_K(KV_NEXT(base / BN + 1u)) }
#define KV_AFTER_S { KV_BARRIER STORE_K FETCH_V(KV_NEXT(base / BN + 1u)) }
#define KV_AFTER_O { KV_BARRIER STORE_V }
'''
s=s.replace(old,new,1)
s=s.replace('''#else
#define KV_AFTER_S
#define KV_AFTER_O
#endif''','''#else
#define KV_BEFORE_S
#define KV_AFTER_S
#define KV_AFTER_O
#endif''',1)
s=s.replace('''// the sixteen lanes of a ds_load_b64). One plane each, so two barriers a
// block: after the S^T reads (K's plane is rewritten behind it) and after
// the O^T reads (V's).''','''// the sixteen lanes of a ds_load_b64). One plane each, so two barriers a
// block: after the S^T reads (K's plane is rewritten behind it) and after
// the O^T reads (V's).''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='h3_attn_t_block.glsl'
s=open(p).read()
old='''        // ---- S^T = K . Q^T.
        ACC s[QT][KTIL];'''
new='''        KV_BEFORE_S

        // ---- S^T = K . Q^T.
        ACC s[QT][KTIL];'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

cd /home/kube/repos/strix-halo-vulkan/shaders && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='h3_attn_t.comp'
s=open(p).read()
old=s[s.index('    FETCH_K(0u)\n'):s.index('#else\n#define KV_AFTER_S\n')]
new='''    FETCH_K(0u)
    FETCH_V(0u)
    STORE_K
    STORE_V
    barrier();
    // A block fetches the next block's K at its top, in flight behind its
    // S^T MMAs, and writes it to the plane behind the barrier that ends
    // their reads; then V likewise behind the softmax and the O^T MMAs.
    // Fetched and stored inside one trip: a staging register carried across
    // the back-edge is copied there, behind a wait for the fetch (the
    // first cut's disassembly, research/3.9). At the last block the fetches
    // re-read it (in bounds, never read back).
#define KV_BEFORE_S { FETCH_K(KV_NEXT(base / BN + 1u)) }
#define KV_AFTER_S { KV_BARRIER STORE_K FETCH_V(KV_NEXT(base / BN + 1u)) }
#define KV_AFTER_O { KV_BARRIER STORE_V }
'''
s=s.replace(old,new,1)
s=s.replace('''#else
#define KV_AFTER_S
#define KV_AFTER_O
#endif''','''#else
#define KV_BEFORE_S
#define KV_AFTER_S
#define KV_AFTER_O
#endif''',1)
s=s.replace('''// the sixteen lanes of a ds_load_b64). One plane each, so two barriers a
// block: after the S^T reads (K's plane is rewritten behind it) and after
// the O^T reads (V's).''','''// the sixteen lanes of a ds_load_b64). One plane each, so two barriers a
// block: after the S^T reads (K's plane is rewritten behind it) and after
// the O^T reads (V's).''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='h3_attn_t_block.glsl'
s=open(p).read()
old='''        // ---- S^T = K . Q^T.
        ACC s[QT][KTIL];'''
new='''        KV_BEFORE_S

        // ---- S^T = K . Q^T.
        ACC s[QT][KTIL];'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

B="glslc --target-env=vulkan1.2 -O -I. -DKVLDS=1 -DQT=1 -DKTIL=4"
$B -DWAVES=8 -o $S/k2_base.spv h3_attn_t.comp &&
$B -DWAVES=8 -DLAZY=1 -o $S/k2_lz.spv h3_attn_t.comp &&
$B -DWAVES=8 -DMAX_TREE=1 -DLAZY=1 -DTAIL_SPLIT=1 -o $S/k2_tml.spv h3_attn_t.comp &&
$B -DWAVES=8 -DMAX_TREE=1 -DLAZY=1 -DTAIL_SPLIT=1 -DKV_STAGE_L0=1 -o $S/k2_tml_l0.spv h3_attn_t.comp &&

$B -DWAVES=16 -DLAZY=1 -o $S/k2_w16_lz.spv h3_attn_t.comp &&
for f in k2_base k2_lz k2_tml k2_w16_q0_lz k2_w16_lz; do MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DISABLE=1 RADV_DEBUG=asm,shaderstats $S/probe $S/$f.spv 32 > $S/$f.asm 2>&1; echo "== $f $(grep -E "^VGPRs|Spilled VGPRs|Subgroups|Pre-Sched VGPRs" $S/$f.asm | tr '\n' ' ') moves: $(grep -c -E "v_mov_b32|v_swap|v_mov_b16" $S/$f.asm) dual: $(grep -c v_dual_mov $S/$f.asm)"; done

[← IDEAS.md](ideas.md) · [research index](README.md) · the attention's key blocks through LDS

### 3.9 The attention's K/V blocks staged through LDS for eight waves: 1.10–1.14x on the kernel, bit-identical, a 480p forward 25.2 → 24.3 s — **done** ✅ (2026-09-30)

**Question** (KERNELS.md G4b, left by §3.8): the transposed attention
(`h3_attn_t_qt2_kt4`, one wave32 a workgroup, 32 queries) loads every K
and V fragment of every key block itself, 128 fragment loads beside 128
MMAs, and §3.8 priced those loads at 11–12 points. §2.9's lever on the
GEMM was the slab fetched once a workgroup, ahead, and shared through
LDS. §3.8 estimated it here at "the 12 memory points less 6–9 of LDS reads
and barrier, ≤ 2% of a forward" and did not build it. Is that the number?

**Answer: it is 10–14% on the kernel and 3.7% on a forward, bit-identical,
and it ships for `h3/dit`.** The estimate missed two things: the build is
spill-free at one query tile a wave, so §3.8's exact softmax knobs
(`LAZY`, `TAIL_SPLIT`) — dead at 256 VGPRs with 112 spilled — are worth
6–10% on it; and the fetch is a quarter of the bytes, which the clock
shows (2657 → 2717 MHz over a forward).

| 480p forward, int8 bank, two runs each, interleaved | attention (100 dispatches) | forward | sclk |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| the one-wave build (`H3_ATTN_LDS=0`) | 9.79 / 9.82 s, 37.1–37.2 TFLOP/s | 25.23 / 25.21 s | 2653–2660 MHz |
| **`h3_attn_t_kvlds_w8_kt4`** | **8.91 / 8.90 s, 40.8–40.9 TFLOP/s (1.10x)** | **24.27 / 24.35 s (1.037x)** | 2717–2718 MHz |
| 768p, one run each | 60.5 → **54.3 s** (34.6 → 38.6 TFLOP/s, 1.115x) | 95.9 → **92.5 s** (1.037x) | 2658 → 2704 MHz |

Every new-build forward is bit-identical to the control's
(`H3_GEMM_REF`, both shapes); `TestGPUForward` and `TestGPURun` pass on
the new default.

#### The build

`-DKVLDS=1 -DWAVES=8 -DQT=1 -DKTIL=4 -DLAZY=1 -DTAIL_SPLIT=1` on
`h3_attn_t.comp`. A workgroup is eight wave32 waves, a query tile each
(128 queries), over one head. A key block (64 keys) is 16 KB of K and
16 KB of V^T; the workgroup's 256 lanes fetch each as four `uvec4` a lane
and write them to two LDS planes:

- K: 64 key rows of the head's 128 components at a pitch of 132 halves;
- V^T: 128 component rows of the block's 64 keys at a pitch of 68 halves;

both 2 dwords mod 32, so the sixteen lanes of a fragment's `ds_load_b64`
land on sixteen different bank pairs (§2.9 item 3). 34.8 KB of LDS, one
workgroup a CU, four waves a SIMD, 256 VGPRs, nothing spilled.

One plane each — two K planes and two V planes are 68.6 KB and the limit
is 64 — so a block has two barriers, not the GEMM's one:

```
top of block b:   fetch K(b+1) into 16 staging registers
S^T = K(b).Q^T    32 MMAs, fragments from the K plane
barrier           every wave is done with K(b)
store K(b+1); fetch V(b+1)
softmax
O^T += V(b)^T.P^T 32 MMAs, fragments from the V plane
barrier           every wave is done with V(b)
store V(b+1)
```

Each fetch is in flight for half a block (32 MMAs, 544 clocks, the
GEMM's slab depth) and is fetched and stored inside one trip of the loop.
The same MMAs in the same order per accumulator as the one-wave build at
the same `KTIL`, so the context is the same bits; a wave whose queries
start past the sequence runs the loop (the barriers need it) and stores
nothing.

#### The ladder (the screen, 480p, 15,936 keys, every exact arm bit-identical to the shipped one-wave build)

`TestGPUAttentionScreen` now runs an arm `H3_SCREEN_REPS` times in one
submission and logs the window, so the 100 ms sampler has a busy stretch
an arm: the attention alone runs at 2450–2600 MHz and 143–149 W. The
medians move ±2% between windows, so the arms are compared in ms inside
one run. The one-wave build read 193.8–197.5 ms across the day's runs.

| arm | ms | |
|---|---:|---|
| the one-wave build, `QT2 KTIL4` | 193.8 – 197.5 | 37.3–37.6 TFLOP/s |
| first cut: both fetches a block ahead, staging registers carried across the back-edge | 196.1 – 200.2 | a tie |
| … with `LAZY` / `MAX_TREE LAZY TAIL_SPLIT` | 187 / 181–185 | §3.8's knobs pay here |
| … no barriers (`KV_NOBAR`) / staging all L0 hits (`KV_STAGE_L0`) | 190–192 / 180–182 | barrier 3%, global side **8–9%** |
| **fetched and stored inside one trip** (above), plain | 193.9 – 194.9 | |
| … `LAZY` / `MAX_TREE LAZY` / `MAX_TREE LAZY TAIL_SPLIT` | 187.4 / 189.6 / 177.7–178.2 | |
| **… `LAZY TAIL_SPLIT` (shipped)** | **175.1 – 175.6** | **41.5 TFLOP/s, 1.11x** |
| … its controls: no barriers / staging L0 / softmax gutted | 170.3 / 164.6 / 165.6 | barrier 3%, global ≤ 6%, softmax 6% |
| both fetches at the top, both stores behind the O^T reads, the barriers back to back (`KV_DEEP`) | 193.7 – 194.8 with every knob | the back-to-back barriers cost what the depth buys |
| V fetched at the top too (`KV_VTOP`) | 182.8 | 16 more live registers |
| the first barrier behind the softmax (`KV_BSOFT`), and with `KV_VTOP` | 184.1 / 188.4 | |
| sixteen waves a workgroup (capped at 192 VGPRs: 26–35 spilled with Q^T in registers) | 185.7 – 202 | |
| sixteen waves, Q^T re-read (`QREG=0`, spill-free) | 196 – 200 | Q's loads are exposed |
| eight waves, `QREG=0` | 220 | |
| `KTIL2` (18 KB of LDS, 192 VGPRs; not bit-identical, a different softmax blocking) | 199.7 | |

At 768p (38,247 keys): 1.195 → **1.046 s** (35.1 → 40.1 TFLOP/s, 1.14x);
`MAX_TREE LAZY TAIL_SPLIT` 1.063, `LAZY` alone 1.126, sixteen waves 1.135.
At 192×320 (3,100 keys, 124 frames): 7.58 → **7.05 ms** (1.07x), so the
build does not need a long sequence (its grid is rows/128 × 56 heads).

#### What it says

1. **A register carried across a loop's back-edge is copied there, behind
   a wait for whatever it holds.** The first cut fetched a block ahead
   into staging registers that lived across the back-edge. The
   disassembly: the new fetch is issued into fresh registers, and the
   back-edge copies them into the phi's registers behind
   `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)` — so every block waited out its own fetch, and
   the "block ahead" was no prefetch at all (8–9% by the L0 control).
   §2.9 found the same thing about fragments; it is true of plain `uvec4`
   too. The GEMM's staging has always been fetched and stored inside one
   trip, which is why it never showed. The same back-edge also rotated
   all 64 accumulator registers (37 `v_dual_mov`), which the restructure
   removed with it: the whole-block loop of the shipped build is 339
   non-MMA VALU beside 64 MMAs, 5.3 an MMA against the one-wave build's
   7.1, with ~160 moves.
2. **The exact knobs were dead only at the register limit.** §3.8 measured
   `LAZY`, `MAX_TREE` and `TAIL_SPLIT` inside ±2% on the one-wave build
   and concluded the allocator's moves redraw with every edit. On a build
   at 222 of 256 VGPRs with nothing spilled, `LAZY` (skip the rescale of
   O^T when no lane's max moved) is 3–4% and `TAIL_SPLIT` another 6%;
   `MAX_TREE` still loses. The allocator still decides: the three-knob
   build reads 131 + 136 moves in its disassembly and is 1.5% slower
   than the two-knob one.
3. **Two barriers a block cost 3%**, less than the GEMM's 6–9 for one a
   slab: the softmax between them is VALU work every wave does anyway.
4. **The fetch is a quarter of the bytes.** 32 KB a block for 128 queries
   where the one-wave build moved 32 KB for 32, and the forward's clock
   rises 60 MHz at the same package power.

**What is left in the kernel**, by the shipped build's controls: the
softmax 6%, the global side ≤ 6% (the L0 control also never moves a max,
so `LAZY` skips every rescale in it: an upper bound), the barriers 3%.
The three arms on the fetch's depth and the barrier's place all lost.

#### Carry-in

- **`h3/dit`: the default** wherever the transposed kernel runs
  (`AttnVariant{QT: 8, KTIL: 4, T: true}`; `QT` is query tiles a
  workgroup). `H3_ATTN_LDS=0` on `TestGPUShapes` is the control.
- **`h3/vae`: priced and left.** The head-64 build
  (`-DHEAD_DIM=64 -DSTORE_TAIL=0`, 17 KB of LDS, 192 VGPRs) reads 6.10 ms
  against the shipped `QT2 KTIL4`'s 6.22 on the VAE's screen (8 × 1,808
  keys), and two query tiles a wave 6.88: inside the screen's spread, on
  a kernel that is 14.5 VALU an MMA and a few percent of a decode. Not
  embedded.
- **`qimage/dit`: not carried.** Its transposed attention is opt-in behind
  the edit gate (§3.8) and this build is the same bits, so the gate's
  verdict is the same; the build would apply as it stands
  (`-DSTORE_TAIL=0`) if that gate is settled.

**Reproduce.** The generate line is in `shaders/shaders.go`
(`h3_attn_t_kvlds_w8_kt4`). The screen: `H3_SCREEN=480x864 H3_BANK=q8
H3_ATTN_ONLY_SPV=1 H3_SCREEN_REPS=12 H3_ATTN_SPV=8:4:arm.spv,…` on
`TestGPUAttentionScreen`, where the first field is now the query tiles a
*workgroup* (8 for eight waves of `QT=1`, 16 for sixteen); each line ends
in `window <from> <to>` in epoch milliseconds for a sampler. Knobs on
`h3_attn_t.comp`: `KVLDS`, `WAVES`, `K_LPITCH`, `V_LPITCH`, the exact arms
`KV_DEEP`, `KV_VTOP`, `KV_BSOFT`, and the controls `KV_NOBAR`,
`KV_STAGE_L0` (wrong by construction). The forward: `H3_SHAPES=480
H3_PROFILE=1 H3_BANK=q8 H3_GEMM_REF=ref.bits [H3_ATTN_LDS=0]` on
`TestGPUShapes`, the control first so it writes the reference.

<!-- §3.9 — KERNELS.md G4b. The section number is the stable identifier
     cited from shaders/, h3/ and the root docs. Do not renumber it. -->

[← IDEAS.md](ideas.md) · [research index](README.md) · the attention's key blocks through LDS

### 3.9 The attention's K/V blocks staged through LDS for eight waves: 1.10–1.14x on the kernel, bit-identical, a 480p forward 25.2 → 24.3 s — **done** ✅ (2026-09-30)

**Question** (KERNELS.md G4b, left by §3.8): the transposed attention
(`h3_attn_t_qt2_kt4`, one wave32 a workgroup, 32 queries) loads every K
and V fragment of every key block itself, 128 fragment loads beside 128
MMAs, and §3.8 priced those loads at 11–12 points. §2.9's lever on the
GEMM was the slab fetched once a workgroup, ahead, and shared through
LDS. §3.8 estimated it here at "the 12 memory points less 6–9 of LDS reads
and barrier, ≤ 2% of a forward" and did not build it. Is that the number?

**Answer: it is 10–14% on the kernel and 3.7% on a forward, bit-identical,
and it ships for `h3/dit`.** The estimate missed two things: the build is
spill-free at one query tile a wave, so §3.8's exact softmax knobs
(`LAZY`, `TAIL_SPLIT`) — dead at 256 VGPRs with 112 spilled — are worth
6–10% on it; and the fetch is a quarter of the bytes, which the clock
shows (2657 → 2717 MHz over a forward).

| 480p forward, int8 bank, two runs each, interleaved | attention (100 dispatches) | forward | sclk |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| the one-wave build (`H3_ATTN_LDS=0`) | 9.79 / 9.82 s, 37.1–37.2 TFLOP/s | 25.23 / 25.21 s | 2653–2660 MHz |
| **`h3_attn_t_kvlds_w8_kt4`** | **8.91 / 8.90 s, 40.8–40.9 TFLOP/s (1.10x)** | **24.27 / 24.35 s (1.037x)** | 2717–2718 MHz |
| 768p, one run each | 60.5 → **54.3 s** (34.6 → 38.6 TFLOP/s, 1.115x) | 95.9 → **92.5 s** (1.037x) | 2658 → 2704 MHz |

Every new-build forward is bit-identical to the control's
(`H3_GEMM_REF`, both shapes); `TestGPUForward` and `TestGPURun` pass on
the new default.

#### The build

`-DKVLDS=1 -DWAVES=8 -DQT=1 -DKTIL=4 -DLAZY=1 -DTAIL_SPLIT=1` on
`h3_attn_t.comp`. A workgroup is eight wave32 waves, a query tile each
(128 queries), over one head. A key block (64 keys) is 16 KB of K and
16 KB of V^T; the workgroup's 256 lanes fetch each as four `uvec4` a lane
and write them to two LDS planes:

- K: 64 key rows of the head's 128 components at a pitch of 132 halves;
- V^T: 128 component rows of the block's 64 keys at a pitch of 68 halves;

both 2 dwords mod 32, so the sixteen lanes of a fragment's `ds_load_b64`
land on sixteen different bank pairs (§2.9 item 3). 34.8 KB of LDS, one
workgroup a CU, four waves a SIMD, 256 VGPRs, nothing spilled.

One plane each — two K planes and two V planes are 68.6 KB and the limit
is 64 — so a block has two barriers, not the GEMM's one:

```
top of block b:   fetch K(b+1) into 16 staging registers
S^T = K(b).Q^T    32 MMAs, fragments from the K plane
barrier           every wave is done with K(b)
store K(b+1); fetch V(b+1)
softmax
O^T += V(b)^T.P^T 32 MMAs, fragments from the V plane
barrier           every wave is done with V(b)
store V(b+1)
```

Each fetch is in flight for half a block (32 MMAs, 544 clocks, the
GEMM's slab depth) and is fetched and stored inside one trip of the loop.
The same MMAs in the same order per accumulator as the one-wave build at
the same `KTIL`, so the context is the same bits; a wave whose queries
start past the sequence runs the loop (the barriers need it) and stores
nothing.

#### The ladder (the screen, 480p, 15,936 keys, every exact arm bit-identical to the shipped one-wave build)

`TestGPUAttentionScreen` now runs an arm `H3_SCREEN_REPS` times in one
submission and logs the window, so the 100 ms sampler has a busy stretch
an arm: the attention alone runs at 2450–2600 MHz and 143–149 W. The
medians move ±2% between windows, so the arms are compared in ms inside
one run. The one-wave build read 193.8–197.5 ms across the day's runs.

| arm | ms | |
|---|---:|---|
| the one-wave build, `QT2 KTIL4` | 193.8 – 197.5 | 37.3–37.6 TFLOP/s |
| first cut: both fetches a block ahead, staging registers carried across the back-edge | 196.1 – 200.2 | a tie |
| … with `LAZY` / `MAX_TREE LAZY TAIL_SPLIT` | 187 / 181–185 | §3.8's knobs pay here |
| … no barriers (`KV_NOBAR`) / staging all L0 hits (`KV_STAGE_L0`) | 190–192 / 180–182 | barrier 3%, global side **8–9%** |
| **fetched and stored inside one trip** (above), plain | 193.9 – 194.9 | |
| … `LAZY` / `MAX_TREE LAZY` / `MAX_TREE LAZY TAIL_SPLIT` | 187.4 / 189.6 / 177.7–178.2 | |
| **… `LAZY TAIL_SPLIT` (shipped)** | **175.1 – 175.6** | **41.5 TFLOP/s, 1.11x** |
| … its controls: no barriers / staging L0 / softmax gutted | 170.3 / 164.6 / 165.6 | barrier 3%, global ≤ 6%, softmax 6% |
| both fetches at the top, both stores behind the O^T reads, the barriers back to back (`KV_DEEP`) | 193.7 – 194.8 with every knob | the back-to-back barriers cost what the depth buys |
| V fetched at the top too (`KV_VTOP`) | 182.8 | 16 more live registers |
| the first barrier behind the softmax (`KV_BSOFT`), and with `KV_VTOP` | 184.1 / 188.4 | |
| sixteen waves a workgroup (capped at 192 VGPRs: 26–35 spilled with Q^T in registers) | 185.7 – 202 | |
| sixteen waves, Q^T re-read (`QREG=0`, spill-free) | 196 – 200 | Q's loads are exposed |
| eight waves, `QREG=0` | 220 | |
| `KTIL2` (18 KB of LDS, 192 VGPRs; not bit-identical, a different softmax blocking) | 199.7 | |

At 768p (38,247 keys): 1.195 → **1.046 s** (35.1 → 40.1 TFLOP/s, 1.14x);
`MAX_TREE LAZY TAIL_SPLIT` 1.063, `LAZY` alone 1.126, sixteen waves 1.135.
At 192×320 (3,100 keys, 124 frames): 7.58 → **7.05 ms** (1.07x), so the
build does not need a long sequence (its grid is rows/128 × 56 heads).

#### What it says

1. **A register carried across a loop's back-edge is copied there, behind
   a wait for whatever it holds.** The first cut fetched a block ahead
   into staging registers that lived across the back-edge. The
   disassembly: the new fetch is issued into fresh registers, and the
   back-edge copies them into the phi's registers behind
   `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)` — so every block waited out its own fetch, and
   the "block ahead" was no prefetch at all (8–9% by the L0 control).
   §2.9 found the same thing about fragments; it is true of plain `uvec4`
   too. The GEMM's staging has always been fetched and stored inside one
   trip, which is why it never showed. The same back-edge also rotated
   all 64 accumulator registers (37 `v_dual_mov`), which the restructure
   removed with it: the whole-block loop of the shipped build is 339
   non-MMA VALU beside 64 MMAs, 5.3 an MMA against the one-wave build's
   7.1, with ~160 moves.
2. **The exact knobs were dead only at the register limit.** §3.8 measured
   `LAZY`, `MAX_TREE` and `TAIL_SPLIT` inside ±2% on the one-wave build
   and concluded the allocator's moves redraw with every edit. On a build
   at 222 of 256 VGPRs with nothing spilled, `LAZY` (skip the rescale of
   O^T when no lane's max moved) is 3–4% and `TAIL_SPLIT` another 6%;
   `MAX_TREE` still loses. The allocator still decides: the three-knob
   build reads 131 + 136 moves in its disassembly and is 1.5% slower
   than the two-knob one.
3. **Two barriers a block cost 3%**, less than the GEMM's 6–9 for one a
   slab: the softmax between them is VALU work every wave does anyway.
4. **The fetch is a quarter of the bytes.** 32 KB a block for 128 queries
   where the one-wave build moved 32 KB for 32, and the forward's clock
   rises 60 MHz at the same package power.

**What is left in the kernel**, by the shipped build's controls: the
softmax 6%, the global side ≤ 6% (the L0 control also never moves a max,
so `LAZY` skips every rescale in it: an upper bound), the barriers 3%.
The three arms on the fetch's depth and the barrier's place all lost.

#### Carry-in

- **`h3/dit`: the default** wherever the transposed kernel runs
  (`AttnVariant{QT: 8, KTIL: 4, T: true}`; `QT` is query tiles a
  workgroup). `H3_ATTN_LDS=0` on `TestGPUShapes` is the control.
- **`h3/vae`: priced and left.** The head-64 build
  (`-DHEAD_DIM=64 -DSTORE_TAIL=0`, 17 KB of LDS, 192 VGPRs) reads 6.10 ms
  against the shipped `QT2 KTIL4`'s 6.22 on the VAE's screen (8 × 1,808
  keys), and two query tiles a wave 6.88: inside the screen's spread, on
  a kernel that is 14.5 VALU an MMA and a few percent of a decode. Not
  embedded.
- **`qimage/dit`: not carried.** Its transposed attention is opt-in behind
  the edit gate (§3.8) and this build is the same bits, so the gate's
  verdict is the same; the build would apply as it stands
  (`-DSTORE_TAIL=0`) if that gate is settled.

**Reproduce.** The generate line is in `shaders/shaders.go`
(`h3_attn_t_kvlds_w8_kt4`). The screen: `H3_SCREEN=480x864 H3_BANK=q8
H3_ATTN_ONLY_SPV=1 H3_SCREEN_REPS=12 H3_ATTN_SPV=8:4:arm.spv,…` on
`TestGPUAttentionScreen`, where the first field is now the query tiles a
*workgroup* (8 for eight waves of `QT=1`, 16 for sixteen); each line ends
in `window <from> <to>` in epoch milliseconds for a sampler. Knobs on
`h3_attn_t.comp`: `KVLDS`, `WAVES`, `K_LPITCH`, `V_LPITCH`, the exact arms
`KV_DEEP`, `KV_VTOP`, `KV_BSOFT`, and the controls `KV_NOBAR`,
`KV_STAGE_L0` (wrong by construction). The forward: `H3_SHAPES=480
H3_PROFILE=1 H3_BANK=q8 H3_GEMM_REF=ref.bits [H3_ATTN_LDS=0]` on
`TestGPUShapes`, the control first so it writes the reference.

---
name: attention-kernel-plateau
description: The transposed WMMA attention (h3_attn_t.comp) is at a measured plateau — no exact arm beats the shipped build; how it decomposes (softmax 7, K/V loads 12, floor 81%), why the allocator's moves decide, and the image DiT's edit gate that sits near its sensitivity floor.
metadata:
  type: project
---

KERNELS.md G4 / research §3.8 (2026-09-30): `h3_attn_t_qt2_kt4` runs at 73% per clock (37.3–37.8 TFLOP/s at 480p, 2650–2690 MHz). Gutting it honestly (results kept live, `GUT_*` knobs) puts the MMA+loads floor at 81%, 87–90% with every K/V load an L0 hit (`L0_LOADS`); the softmax is 6–7 points (the row max's 16-deep chain 7, the rescale 3), the K/V loads 11–12. Five bit-identical arms (`TAIL_SPLIT`, `QLDS`, `MAX_TREE`, `LAZY`, `PV_ORDER`) all land within ±2% of the shipped build at 480p and 768p — the best executes 135 fewer VALU and no spill reloads a block for the same time. Head split (1.5x MMAs) and wave64 (VALU two passes) are dead by arithmetic. The one lever left is G4b: K/V slabs staged through LDS for a workgroup's waves at QT1 (§2.9's lever), ≤ 2% of a video forward.

**Why:** at 256 VGPRs the register allocator's ~200–390 moves a block redraw with every source edit and cost what the edit saves; the instruction count is an upper bound, not a price (as §2.13 found on the MoE GEMM). Screen arms against the shipped build's *time*, not its counts.

**How to apply:** don't build more exact arms on this kernel without a structural register change; the screen is `TestGPUAttentionScreen` with `H3_ATTN_ONLY_SPV=1 H3_ATTN_SPV=qt:ktil:path` (it reports "bits: identical" against the shipped transposed build). On the image DiT the kernel is opt-in (`QIMAGE_ATTN_T=1`): exact on identical inputs (rms 8e-5 a block), but `TestGPUEditOracle`'s prefill bound (2e-2) amplifies prefix-row fp16 differences ~100x at three target rows — a plain-family perturbation reads 1.73e-2, the transposed 7.9e-2. Before blaming a kernel on a gate like that, perturb the passing path with a same-family build and dump the context block by block (the kernel run at one block alone on the other kernel's inputs is the decisive test). See [[valu-costs-matrix-clocks]], [[coopmat-fragments-cost-8-vgprs]], [[h3-gemm-screen-recipe]].
---
name: coopmat-fragments-cost-8-vgprs
description: "A wave64 WMMA A/B fragment is 8 VGPRs (4x replicated), ACO copies any fragment carried across a loop back-edge element by element, and LDS coopmat reads are ds_load_b64; what that rules out for the GEMM."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 52025e37-e99f-41af-81f6-04ea3d9309c8
  modified: 2026-09-29T20:14:13.732Z
---

Three compiler/hardware facts about cooperative matrices on this part (Mesa 26.2.2 RADV, RDNA3.5), established in KERNELS.md G2 / research §2.9 (2026-09-29):

- A 16x16 fp16 A or B fragment is **8 VGPRs at wave64 and at wave32** (the hardware replicates it across the 16-lane groups: 4x at wave64, 2x at wave32), and a fragment load moves 4x (2x) its 512 B through L0→VGPR. The accumulator is 4 VGPRs at wave64, 8 at wave32.
- **ACO cannot coalesce a coopmat carried across a loop back-edge**: it copies it as ~16 `v_mov_b16`. Any register double-buffering / software pipelining of fragments across K tiles compiles to hundreds of moves a trip and loses. Only shapes that carry nothing (a hoisted multi-tile slab, or LDS staging) measure a prefetch.
- `coopMatLoad` from `shared` lowers to four `ds_load_b64` per fragment, for which the LDS serves 16 lanes a clock: the conflict-free row/column pitch is 36 halves (18 dwords), not 24 (16-lane 2-way) and not 16 (4-way).

**Why:** §6.5 planned a "+24 VGPR" register prefetch that was really +96 and then un-coalescable; two arms were dead before they ran. The shipped GEMM (`dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32`) is LDS-staged slabs at wave32 because of exactly these three facts.

**How to apply:** don't build cross-iteration register pipelines of coopmat operands on this Mesa; read `RADV_DEBUG=asm` for `v_mov_b16` counts before timing any loop that carries fragments; LDS fragment pitches are 36 halves. See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and [[h3-gemm-screen-recipe]].

content.text:
KERNELS.md listed three candidates as next (G4b, G7, the rest of G6); I took the first, **G4b**, and it is done: the attention's K/V blocks now go through LDS, and a 480p video forward is 25.2 → 24.3 s, bit-identical.

## What shipped

`h3_attn_t_kvlds_w8_kt4` is the new default attention in `h3/dit`. A workgroup is eight wave32 waves sharing each key block. K and V are fetched once per workgroup, half a block ahead, into one LDS plane each. The build is spill-free.

| | one-wave build (control) | new build |
|---|---:|---:|
| attention in a 480p forward | 9.79 / 9.82 s, 37.2 TFLOP/s | 8.91 / 8.90 s, 40.8 TFLOP/s (1.10x) |
| 480p forward | 25.23 / 25.21 s | 24.27 / 24.35 s (1.037x) |
| 768p forward (one run each) | 95.9 s | 92.5 s |
| attention in a 768p forward | 60.5 s | 54.3 s (1.115x) |
| clock during the 480p forward | 2653–2660 MHz | 2717–2718 MHz |
| per clock | 73% | 78% |

Gates: forwards are bit-identical to the control at both shapes (`H3_GEMM_REF`), and `TestGPUForward` and `TestGPURun` pass on the new default. The default builds of `h3_attn_t.comp` compile to byte-identical SPIR-V as before the edit.

## What I found on the way

- **The first cut only tied the old build.** Its staging registers were carried across the loop back-edge, and the compiler copies them there behind a wait for the fetch, so the "block ahead" prefetch was waited out every block. Fetching and storing inside one trip of the loop fixed it.
- **§3.8's exact softmax knobs pay on this build.** `LAZY` and `TAIL_SPLIT` were inside ±2% on the spilled one-wave build; here `LAZY` is 3–4% and `TAIL_SPLIT` about 6% more. `MAX_TREE` still loses.
- **§3.8's estimate of ≤ 2% of a forward was low.** It had the LDS-side cost right (the two barriers are 3%) but missed the knobs and the clock gain from fetching a quarter of the bytes.
- **Dead arms, measured:** both fetches a whole block deep, V fetched at the top, the barrier behind the softmax, sixteen waves a workgroup, Q re-read from memory, and `KTIL2`.
- **Left in the kernel by its controls:** softmax 6%, global side ≤ 6%, barriers 3%.

## Not carried

- **Video VAE:** the head-64 build read 6.10 ms against 6.22 on its screen, inside the spread, so I removed it again.
- **Image DiT:** its transposed attention is still opt-in behind the edit gate, and this build is the same bits, so nothing changes there.

## Things to know

- The served binary still needs a redeploy (already pending since G3; this one needs no restaging).
- Nothing is committed; the changes sit in the working tree alongside the earlier sessions' uncommitted work.
- The screen's first `H3_ATTN_SPV` field now means query tiles per workgroup (8 for this build), and `H3_SCREEN_REPS` repeats an arm inside one submission so the clock sampler gets a busy window. `H3_ATTN_LDS=0` on `TestGPUShapes` is the control.
- The clock sampler is still a scratchpad script, and the raw screen logs are in the session scratchpad only.

The record is in `research/3.9-attention-kv-lds.md`, with KERNELS.md (stage row, section, handoff), TODO.md, VIDEO.md and the research index updated. Next per the handoff: G7 (the CPU's share of the power budget, and the sampler into `bench/sysmon.go`) or the rest of G6.
